This and this is what made me think about it. As most communities/subverses are small, there are few rules in place regarding content types and for now it is pragmatic solution given the small size of it. Niche subverses don't have much traction at this stage since the number of subscribers are going to be even smaller and there won't be much activity. Even if such subverses exist, people are going to post content in the main ones because that is where it will get the most views.

 

Hubski uses tags exclusively instead of subverses. It has a different dynamic and I dont think it will work in quite the same manner as Voat or Reddit.

But, that same idea could be used within subverses. When a user subscribes to a subverse, he/she will be subscribed to all the tags in the sub.

For example: One of the tags in /v/funny could be meme. By default a user will be subscribed to all tags. If after a while he/she is getting annoyed by all the memes; they can just unsubscribe the "meme" tag instead of unsubbing from /v/funny or the mods having to ban it, which is what would happen in the current state.

Mods can pick tags and users will be made to input a tag along with subverse name when they are posting content. I am not suggesting cross subverse/global tags like hubski, just tags within a subverse.

 

I think it will solve a pain point regarding subs being taken over by the masses and content quality going down after it crosses a subscriber threshold.

The original subscribers that are here now will not need to unsub in the future and go to smaller subs. It is an inclusive idea and might reduce complaints regarding content posted in subs, which is a frequent area of friction between users and also mods.

I don't see this affecting niche subs as people like to form communities with others of similar interests.
